title: Israel orders evacuation of northern Gaza south of Wadi Gaza
body:
On 13 October 2023, the Israel Defense Forces told the United Nations that the roughly 1.1 million people living north of Wadi Gaza, including Gaza City, should relocate to southern Gaza. Reports differ on the deadline: the UN said it was given 24 hours, while some accounts describe a shorter window. The Israeli military said Gaza City was an area where military operations would take place and that residents could return only when permitted.

The UN described the order as impractical to execute safely and said it would have devastating humanitarian consequences. UN spokesman Stéphane Dujarric called it impossible and urged that it be rescinded. The order also applied to UN staff and people sheltering in UN facilities. Over the next two days, hundreds of thousands of people moved south.

Multiple strikes reportedly hit Palestinians leaving northern Gaza on 13 October, killing about 70 people, mostly women and children, and injuring about 200, according to accounts summarised on Wikipedia. Hamas accused Israel of bombing civilians, while Israel accused Hamas of blocking evacuations and using civilians as human shields. Later, the UN Office for the Coordination of Humanitarian Affairs reported on 6 February 2024 that two-thirds of Gaza, once home to 1.78 million people, was under evacuation orders. The evacuation orders became a recurring feature of the war and were compared by some Palestinians to the 1948 Nakba.
